concepts.text: People gather around a whiteboard, practise at a laptop with guidance, review together and leave with a reusable takeaway.

A team's source examples and quality checklist lie on a tailor's cutting table. A maker fits them into a reusable skill sleeve; test swatches are checked, the packaged tool goes to the team, and customer feedback returns to the fitting table.

An editor's desk turns a messy brief and reference stack into a bound recipe for a recurring task. A proof copy is tested against examples, released into the team's tool drawer, then returned with customer-context annotations.
A tiny factory sends blank paper down a conveyor, through several machines and an approval booth, into a finished-output tray.
A luthier fits a custom instrument to a team's work, tests its sound, hands it to the player and adjusts it after use. A task recipe and source examples sit beside the instrument.
A screen with five numbered rectangular cards connected by arrows and a return arrow from last to second.

A dispatch room routes repeated work envelopes through a CRM cabinet, productivity-app tray and system-of-record archive. A person at a control desk releases a judgment-sensitive handoff to a review window and output dock.

A railway interlocking moves work between three visibly distinct business-system stations. A human signal operator directs the critical junction, a review siding checks the work, and approved output reaches its destination.
Three islands represent CRM, productivity apps and records; a causeway carries repetitive work across them. At the central lock a person reviews the crossing and the usable output lands.
A pneumatic-tube post office carries work capsules between labeled business-system rooms, through a human-operated review hatch to the result tray.
A friendly autonomous robot works overnight at a laptop while humans sleep; every item leaving its belt has an automatic green approval mark.
An executive desk seen across a day: morning briefing folio, meeting preparation card, debrief notes and action slips, ending at the leader's red decision pen.
A compact boardroom with an agenda rail moves from daily brief to meeting brief to debrief and actions. A single senior leader chooses what happens next.
A ship captain at a wheel receives daily dispatches, meeting notes and recommendations; the captain directs the route.
An airport-style departure board shows Critical, Calendar, Pipeline and Actions while a leader rearranges four fictional briefing cards.
A red throne overlooks a factory staffed by small robots, with money bags appearing at the end.

Four role desks inside one company: deal documents, operations queue, product feedback and sales account folder. Each person uses a tailored task tool, reviews their own lane and receives the reviewed work back.
Four tool rolls each shaped around deal, operations, product and sales work; the owner selects a tailored capability, checks its output and continues the role's craft.
A jazz quartet plays different parts from role-specific scores; one review passage resolves into four distinct work outputs for deal, operations, product and sales.
Four people stand in lanes feeding a single giant stamp, after which one shared document appears.
Four people sit at laptops in a workshop while a facilitator points at a board and gives them exercises.

A non-engineer champion works at a proving bench: designs a reusable capability from simple pieces, tests examples, opens a failed piece to troubleshoot, checks anticipated failure cases and hands the reviewed capability to a teammate.
A builder's flight-test hangar shows design drawings, ground tests, a fault inspection, a preflight failure checklist and a capability released for team use. A person signs each review.
A greenhouse shows seeds, growing plants, pruning, pest checks and a mature plant; small cards carry design, test, troubleshoot, anticipate failures and workflow in use.
An escape-room puzzle bench turns tests and failure cards into clues; an AI champion checks and repairs a task system before handing it to colleagues.
A dark hacker terminal displays code while a hooded engineer assembles a robot brain.

classes.description: People learn together on real work through guided practice and group review. Include classroom/whiteboard/keyboard practice. Exclude individual routine workstations without teaching. Example: facilitator watches a team practise.

Expertise, examples and quality standards become a reusable custom Claude skill or plugin, tested and improved in customer context. Include authoring, packaging and refit loops. Exclude cross-system orchestration as principal story. Example: brief is fitted into a reusable skill.

Repetitive work travels between business systems with humans directing or reviewing where judgment matters. Include handoff infrastructure. Exclude building a single reusable task skill as principal story. Example: work passes CRM to productivity system and review.

A senior leader receives briefings, meeting preparation/debriefs and suggested actions during a day and makes the final decision. Exclude generic team collaboration without executive agenda. Example: morning briefing meets decision desk.

Different business roles each use a tailored capability for their own recurring work and retain responsibility for quality. Include differentiated role-specific workstations. Exclude teaching session as principal story. Example: deal, operations, product and sales each handle role work.

Non-engineer AI champions assemble, test, troubleshoot and anticipate failure in a capability before the team uses it. Include practical proving bench. Exclude generic service-delivery process without failure investigation. Example: builder tests pieces and repairs a fault.
The scene lacks sufficient cues to distinguish an owner, or combines two principal stories equally. Takes precedence when no dominant work activity exists. Example: generic boxes connected by arrows.

Four adjacent desks hold a deal folder, an operations plan, product feedback cards and account notes. Four people use different small tools and check their own work along separate lanes that meet a shared review frame.
One person uses a desk with a simple component layout, test examples, an opened failed component and a failure-case checklist, then hands a connected three-piece tool to a teammate.

Repetitive work travels between business systems with humans directing or reviewing where judgment matters. Include handoff infrastructure. Exclude building a single reusable task skill as principal story. Example: work passes CRM to productivity system and review.

A senior leader receives briefings, meeting preparation/debriefs and suggested actions during a day and makes the final decision. Exclude generic team collaboration without executive agenda. Example: morning briefing meets decision desk.

Different business roles each use a tailored capability for their own recurring work and retain responsibility for quality. Include differentiated role-specific workstations. Exclude teaching session as principal story. Example: deal, operations, product and sales each handle role work.

Non-engineer AI champions assemble, test, troubleshoot and anticipate failure in a capability before the team uses it. Include practical proving bench. Exclude generic service-delivery process without failure investigation. Example: builder tests pieces and repairs a fault.
The scene lacks sufficient cues to distinguish an owner, or combines two principal stories equally. Takes precedence when no dominant work activity exists. Example: generic boxes connected by arrows.

One person moves through a morning desk, meeting table, debrief notebook and action tray. A pen in the person's hand marks the final action slips.

Four adjacent desks hold a deal folder, an operations plan, product feedback cards and account notes. Four people use different small tools and check their own work along separate lanes that meet a shared review frame.
One person uses a desk with a simple component layout, test examples, an opened failed component and a failure-case checklist, then hands a connected three-piece tool to a teammate.

args.purpose: Ablation research: choose dominant owner from only the supplied observable scene or words. Sparse office objects do not prove identity. If multiple owners are equally plausible use manual_review.
